flagship.headline: John Lennon privately tells the Beatles he's leaving
flagship.summary_line_1: During a tense meeting at Apple headquarters on September 20, 1969, John Lennon told Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr he was leaving the Beatles, reportedly saying he wanted a divorce, hours after the group signed a new recording contract with EMI and Capitol.
flagship.summary_line_2: At manager Allen Klein's request, Lennon agreed to keep the news quiet to protect the contract, so the public did not learn the Beatles were finished until McCartney announced his own departure the following April.

events.headline: John Lennon privately tells the Beatles he's leaving
events.summary_line_1: During a tense meeting at Apple headquarters on September 20, 1969, John Lennon told Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr he was leaving the Beatles, reportedly saying he wanted a divorce, hours after the group signed a new recording contract with EMI and Capitol.
events.summary_line_2: At manager Allen Klein's request, Lennon agreed to keep the news quiet to protect the contract, so the public did not learn the Beatles were finished until McCartney announced his own departure the following April.

events.headline: The Archies' Sugar, Sugar hits number one
events.summary_line_1: Sugar, Sugar by the cartoon band the Archies, sung by session vocalist Ron Dante, reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 on September 20, 1969, and held the spot for four weeks.
events.summary_line_2: It became the best-selling single of 1969 and the defining bubblegum pop hit of the decade, proof that a studio creation with no real band behind it could still dominate the charts.

events.headline: Blind Faith's debut album hits number one
events.summary_line_1: The self-titled debut album by supergroup Blind Faith, featuring Eric Clapton, Steve Winwood, Ginger Baker, and Ric Grech, reached number one on the Billboard 200 on September 20, 1969.
events.summary_line_2: The band topped the chart with their only record just weeks before they played their final show together, a brief, explosive run typical of the era's short-lived supergroups.

events.headline: The Beatles film the I Am the Walrus sequence at West Malling
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles spent September 20, 1967, on the second day of filming at West Malling air station in Kent, shooting the outdoor I Am the Walrus sequence in psychedelic costumes alongside a walrus, an Eggman, and a troupe of policemen, plus indoor scenes for the magicians' laboratory and Blue Jay Way.
events.summary_line_2: The footage became some of the most surreal imagery of their career once it aired in the Magical Mystery Tour television special that December.

events.headline: George Harrison grants an exclusive BBC interview in Bombay
events.summary_line_1: A day after holding a press conference at Bombay's Taj Mahal Hotel, George Harrison sat down on September 20, 1966, for an exclusive BBC radio interview with correspondent Donald Milner, discussing his sitar lessons under Ravi Shankar.
events.summary_line_2: Traveling under the alias Mr. Sam Wells to dodge the crush of Beatlemania, Harrison used the interview to describe the Eastern philosophy and music that would soon surface on songs like Love You To.

events.headline: Judy Garland guest-stars on The Andy Williams Show
events.summary_line_1: NBC broadcast an episode of The Andy Williams Show on September 20, 1965, featuring Judy Garland as the special guest, opening with a duet of On a Wonderful Day Like Today before she ran through Get Happy, The Trolley Song, and Over the Rainbow.
events.summary_line_2: It was a major prime-time showcase during Garland's celebrated concert years, putting her greatest hits in front of a national television audience just five years after her own variety show had ended.

events.headline: The Who tape a live set at Studio Bellevue in Hilversum
events.summary_line_1: The Who performed a live set for Dutch television at Studio Bellevue in Hilversum, Netherlands, on September 20, 1965, running through early staples like I Can't Explain and Anyway, Anyhow, Anywhere.
events.summary_line_2: The set caught the band's raw mod energy just weeks before My Generation gave them the anthem that would define their sound for the rest of the decade.

events.headline: The Beatles play a fee-waived charity finale at the Paramount Theatre
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles closed their first North American tour on September 20, 1964, with a charity concert at New York's Paramount Theatre, waiving their performance fee to help raise money for United Cerebral Palsy and Retarded Infants Services.
events.summary_line_2: More than 100,000 fans swarmed the streets outside while roughly 200 police officers held the crowd back, a fitting, chaotic bookend to the tour that had just made them America's biggest act.
